machine: closed-die hot forging press, generic die template (not a specific shop)
description: Closed-die (hot) forging of the DN100 valve ball and stem blanks in 2Cr13: wall/feature/gap plus 3 deg die draft, judged by the best-pull-direction draft solver. Grain flow, laps/underfill, flash, die wear and cracks are handoffs; the parting line is not modelled.

source.ref: hot closed-die forging of stainless: ~4 mm minimum web/wall

wallMinMm.detail: Governs webs and flanges, not the ball itself: thinner sections run cold against the die and underfill.

source.ref: small forged ribs/bosses below ~3 mm do not fill; die chill at stainless temperatures

featureMinMm.detail: Die fillet radius (>= 3 mm on the part, larger in the die) has NO rule field in process-profile.schema.json; it is declared here and is a die-design handoff.

source.ref: gaps below ~2 mm between forged features become flash/fill failures; the parting line is not modelled

overhangDeg.reason: Hot forging has no support overhang; the die closes the cavity.

bridgeMaxMm.reason: No unsupported span is created; the die carries the material.

holeAspectMax.reason: Through/blind holes are punched or drilled after forging; the die does not form them.

source.ref: closed-die hot forging draft ~3-7 deg on walls; 3 deg is the floor with good die lubrication

draftMinDeg.detail: Internal draft is usually larger than external. The parting line is not modelled; the solver answers only whether a pull direction exists.

toolRadiusMm.reason: Not a cutting process. Die fillet radii are a die-design rule, declared under featureMinMm and in notes.

source.ref: hot die forging general tolerance ~±0.5 mm for a blank of this size; die wear and thermal contraction dominate

tolMm.detail: A capability; excluding on it needs a tolerance requirement declared elsewhere.

source.ref: as-forged stainless Ra ~3.2-12.5 um, scale included

surfaceRaUm.detail: Reported for information only; never used to exclude.

notes: DRAFT, authored 2026-11-17 for ball-valve-dn100 and NOT calibrated. Process id: the catalog has one forging id (`forging`), which is also the schema `process` family - there is no separate 'die-forging' vocabulary id, so the blank type lives in the profile id `die-forge-2cr13`. Schema gaps stated rather than dropped: (1) die fillet radius (>= 3 mm) has no rule field; (2) machining allowance (1.5-2 mm per machined face on the ball/stem, since the ball seat and stem are ground/machined after forging) has no rule field. Both are handoffs. Forging defects (laps, underfill, flash, die wear, grain flow), heat treatment and the parting line are not mesh-decidable. `not-excluded` means no geometric counter-example was found, never that the blank can be forged.
